purpose: A synthwave horizon: a magenta grid floor rolling toward the viewer one spacing a second, a striped sun whose height follows the day, set below the horizon at night, and the time in cyan segment digits above it.

accent.where: the time digits; the grid, sun and ridge are magenta

night.recipe: The lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes (the Vinyl precedent); the mat around it, visible on the square device, flips with --face-bg, and night dimming comes from the kiosk brightness. For a dark room the glow option pulls the halo in.

options.intent: full is the neon as designed; soft keeps the tubes and their white cores but pulls the halo in, the setting for a clock by the bed.

antiPatterns.rule: Never paint the neon or the stage with --face-ink or --face-bg
antiPatterns.why: the lit disc is content and stays dark in both palettes, like the Vinyl record; the day ink is black and would vanish on it, so only the mat outside the disc reads --face-bg

antiPatterns.rule: Never draw the still parts live every frame
antiPatterns.why: nine glow passes per stroke made the drafts cost 17 to 20 ms a frame at 1080; anything that changes at most once a minute goes through N.layer in src/apps/clock/neon/faces/horizon.ts or the Pi drops frames

antiPatterns.rule: Never let the sun cover the digits
antiPatterns.why: the time is the one cyan quantity; at noon the sun rises highest and must still sit below the numerals

specless: Drawn on a canvas by src/apps/clock/neon/faces/horizon.ts in the shared 1000-unit space. A perspective grid, a striped sun and segment digits have no place in the spec vocabulary of solid hands and two tick rings, so the numbers live in the draw module.
